lines: Gain is how much a stage adds, in decibels. Gain staging is setting every stage so the signal sits clear of the noise and clear of clipping.
Target minus what arrives. Arriving at minus thirty, you want minus eighteen: minus eighteen minus minus thirty — plus twelve. Headroom is what's left above your peaks.
Louder always wins the first listen. Don't let it vote.
…Because I told them.
Hum is the power line singing — sixty hertz here — plus its harmonics: whole-number multiples of it.
Three times sixty. One hundred eighty hertz. A ground loop is how the power line gets into your audio cable in the first place.
So what is it?
Isolate the signal. Never the safety.
The safety ground is never the fix.
Evidence is what you saw or measured, written down before you touch anything. A change record is evidence about what somebody changed.
A label is evidence left for the next person. Worked example: 'MIC 3 → IN 7 · lectern · don't repatch — R.' What it is, where it goes, why it's there.
I label everything. Labels are how the building remembers.

In case it forgets whose it is.
Current is watts divided by volts. A twelve-hundred-watt heater on a hundred-twenty volts draws ten amps.
Plan to eighty percent: a fifteen-amp breaker gives a twelve-amp planning line. The panel is the electrician's. That's a boundary — we bring the numbers, not a screwdriver.
A breaker that trips is the building telling you the truth. Thank it — then call the person who's allowed to listen.
Feedback is the howl when a mic hears its own speaker. Gain before feedback is how loud you can go before it starts.
By minus ten log of how many more. One mic to four: minus ten times log four — about minus six decibels. Mute what nobody's using.
